# Revolution and Romance in Menton: Les Derniers Feux de la royauté

Imagine arriving in Menton in 1789.

There are no grand Belle Époque hotels, no railway along the coast and no palm-lined Promenade du Soleil.

The town is smaller, its streets narrower, its economy shaped by agriculture, maritime trade and its position between larger political powers.

And, most importantly, Menton is not yet part of France.

It's a town associated with the Principality of Monaco, ruled by the Grimaldi dynasty.

Far away in Paris, the French Revolution is beginning to overturn the old order.

What might happen if someone connected to the royal court sought refuge in this small Mediterranean town?

That is the starting point of Les Derniers Feux de la royauté, a historical romance by French author Virginie Platel.

Its heroine, Jeanne Mercier, is a talented portrait painter associated with Marie Antoinette's court.

As revolutionary unrest threatens her familiar world, Jeanne leaves Paris and arrives in Menton.

There she encounters Gabriel, a local man whose political sympathies are very different from her own.

He is drawn to revolutionary ideas.

She has reason to fear them.

Their encounter places two conflicting worlds within the same Mediterranean landscape.

The resulting novel combines romance, personal danger and historical upheaval, while introducing readers to a much less familiar chapter of Menton's past.

This guide explores the historical setting behind the fiction, the real city that inspired it and a short literary walk through streets that still preserve traces of the pre-modern Riviera.

You don't need to read the novel before visiting Menton.

But the book offers a way to imagine the town before it became the international seaside resort we know today.

# Menton à l'heure de la Révolution : Les Derniers Feux de la royauté

Imaginez Menton en 1789 : ni grands hôtels de la Belle Époque, ni chemin de fer côtier, ni promenade du Soleil telle que nous la connaissons. La petite ville vit de l'agriculture, du commerce maritime et de ses relations avec les territoires voisins. Surtout, elle n'est pas française : elle appartient à la principauté de Monaco, sous les Grimaldi.

À Paris, la Révolution ébranle l'ordre ancien. Que devient une artiste liée à la cour lorsqu'elle cherche refuge dans cette ville méditerranéenne ? C'est le point de départ des Derniers Feux de la royauté, roman historique et sentimental de Virginie Platel.

Jeanne Mercier, portraitiste associée à la cour de Marie-Antoinette, quitte Paris et arrive à Menton. Elle y rencontre Gabriel, attiré par les idées révolutionnaires dont elle a, elle, des raisons de se méfier. Leur rencontre rapproche deux univers sociaux et politiques dans un même paysage.

Ce guide propose de découvrir le cadre historique du roman puis de parcourir le centre ancien, sans dévoiler les grands développements de l'intrigue ni son dénouement. Il ne remplace pas une lecture du livre et ne présente pas ses étapes comme les adresses attestées des personnages.

## 2. Why did Virginie Platel choose Menton?

The author has a personal connection with the town.

Virginie Platel was born in Valenciennes, in northern France, but moved to Menton with her family when she was around ten years old.

She attended local schools before studying communication and audiovisual techniques at the University of Nice.

She also studied violin in Menton and Nice and worked professionally as an orchestral musician.

Later, she developed a career as a screenwriter, contributing to French television comedies and programmes for younger audiences.

Her background helps explain the novel's interest in vivid scenes, dialogue and atmosphere.

But her choice of setting was also personal.

When the City of Menton presented Les Derniers Feux de la royauté in October 2020, Platel explained that she wanted to celebrate the town in which she had grown up.

She wanted readers to experience its colours, scents, flavours and history.

### A novelist researching local history

The municipal article provides another significant detail.

Platel consulted the Octobon collection, made available through Menton's municipal library, L'Odyssée, while researching eighteenth-century life.

She acknowledged the assistance of the library's director, Rose-Marie Matton.

This is an important distinction.

The author didn't simply take a modern photograph of Menton and imagine eighteenth-century characters walking through it.

She sought historical material to reconstruct the town's earlier atmosphere.

But historical research and historical accuracy are not identical.

The archives provide a foundation.

The novel turns that material into an imagined story.

## 2. Pourquoi Virginie Platel a-t-elle choisi Menton ?

L'auteure possède un lien personnel avec la ville. Née à Valenciennes, elle arrive à Menton avec sa famille vers l'âge de dix ans. Après le collège la Villa-Blanche et le lycée Pierre-et-Marie-Curie, elle étudie la communication et les techniques audiovisuelles à l'université de Nice.

Elle apprend aussi le violon dans les conservatoires de Menton et de Nice, puis participe à des tournées comme violoniste professionnelle. Devenue scénariste, elle contribue notamment à Un gars, une fille, Scènes de ménages et des fictions pour la jeunesse. Ce parcours éclaire son intérêt pour les scènes, les dialogues et les atmosphères, sans constituer une preuve sur chaque détail du livre.

### Une recherche dans les ressources locales

Dans l'article de la Ville publié le 12 octobre 2020, Platel explique vouloir rendre hommage à la ville où elle a grandi, à ses couleurs, odeurs et saveurs. Elle remercie Rose-Marie Matton, alors directrice de L'Odyssée, pour l'accès au fonds Octobon utilisé dans ses recherches sur le XVIIIe siècle.

Ce travail documentaire distingue le projet d'une simple transposition de la Menton actuelle dans le passé. Il n'en fait pas pour autant une reconstitution infaillible : les archives fournissent une base, le roman construit une histoire imaginée.

L'autrice ha un legame personale con la città. Nata a Valenciennes, vi si trasferisce con la famiglia intorno ai dieci anni. Frequenta il collège la Villa-Blanche e il lycée Pierre-et-Marie-Curie, poi studia comunicazione e tecniche audiovisive all'università di Nizza.

### La ricerca nelle risorse locali

У статті міста від 12 жовтня 2020 року Платель пояснює бажання віддати належне місту дитинства, його барвам, запахам і смакам. Вона дякує Роз-Марі Маттон, тодішній директорці L'Odyssée, за доступ до фонду Octobon для дослідження XVIII століття.

Отже, це не просто сучасна фотографія з уявними персонажами давнини. Історичні матеріали дають основу, а роман перетворює її на вигадану історію. Документальне дослідження й точність кожної сцени не тотожні.

## 3. Menton in 1789: a town that wasn't French

This is the most important historical fact to understand before reading the novel.

Today, Menton is a French town in the Alpes-Maritimes department.

That wasn't its political status when the Revolution began.

Since the fourteenth century, Menton had been associated with Monaco and the Grimaldi dynasty.

By the late eighteenth century, the Principality included Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune.

Its ruler was Prince Honoré III.

France was an influential neighbouring power, but the Principality retained its own political identity.

### A short historical timeline

| Year | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| 1346 | Menton became associated with Charles Grimaldi, Lord of Monaco |
| 1641 | The Treaty of Péronne established French protection over Monaco |
| 1789 | The French Revolution began; Menton was still part of the Principality |
| 1790 | Political reform movements reached Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune |
| 1793 | The Principality's territory was incorporated into revolutionary France |
| 1814 | The Grimaldi dynasty was restored after the Napoleonic period |
| 1848 | Menton and Roquebrune declared themselves free towns under Sardinian protection |
| 1861 | Menton was formally incorporated into France |

This history complicates the usual image of the French Revolution spreading from Paris into an already unified French country.

Menton occupied a politically distinctive position.

Its inhabitants were influenced by events in France, but they also had their own relationships with Monaco, neighbouring Italian territories and the Grimaldi administration.

### Why this matters for the novel

Jeanne arrives from a world in which loyalty to the monarchy is central to her identity and security.

Gabriel represents a different relationship with revolutionary change.

Their conflict becomes more interesting when we remember that the events were not taking place in an ordinary French provincial town.

The political future of the entire region was uncertain.

## 3. Menton en 1789 : une ville qui n'était pas française

Aujourd'hui dans les Alpes-Maritimes, Menton dépendait alors de la principauté de Monaco. Depuis son acquisition par Charles Grimaldi au XIVe siècle, son histoire politique était liée à Monaco et à Roquebrune. À la fin du XVIIIe siècle, Honoré III gouvernait cet ensemble, proche de la France mais doté d'une identité politique distincte.

### Quelques repères historiques

| Année | Événement |
| --- | --- |
| 1346 | Acquisition de Menton par Charles Grimaldi, seigneur de Monaco |
| 1641 | Le traité de Péronne place la principauté sous protection française |
| 1789 | Début de la Révolution ; Menton appartient encore à la principauté |
| 1790 | Des mouvements de réforme touchent Monaco, Menton et Roquebrune |
| 1793 | Le territoire de la principauté est intégré à la France révolutionnaire |
| 1814 | Restauration des Grimaldi après la période napoléonienne |
| 1848 | Menton et Roquebrune se déclarent villes libres sous protection sarde |
| 1861 | Rattachement définitif de Menton à la France |

L'arrivée des idées révolutionnaires ne se déroule donc pas dans une province française ordinaire. Les habitants entretiennent leurs propres liens avec Monaco, les territoires italiens voisins et l'administration des Grimaldi.

### Ce que cela change dans la lecture

Jeanne vient d'un univers où la fidélité à la monarchie conditionne l'identité et la sécurité. Gabriel entretient un autre rapport au changement. Leur opposition prend une dimension particulière dans une région dont l'avenir politique est lui-même incertain.

## 3. Mentone nel 1789: una città che non era francese

Oggi Mentone si trova nelle Alpes-Maritimes, ma all'inizio della Rivoluzione dipendeva dal Principato di Monaco. Dall'acquisizione da parte di Carlo Grimaldi nel Trecento, la sua storia politica era legata a Monaco e Roccabruna. Alla fine del Settecento regnava Onorato III: la Francia esercitava una forte influenza, ma il principato conservava un'identità distinta.

### Una breve cronologia

| Anno | Avvenimento |
| --- | --- |
| 1346 | Mentone viene acquisita da Carlo Grimaldi, signore di Monaco |
| 1641 | Il trattato di Péronne stabilisce la protezione francese sul principato |
| 1789 | Inizia la Rivoluzione; Mentone appartiene ancora al principato |
| 1790 | Movimenti di riforma raggiungono Monaco, Mentone e Roccabruna |
| 1793 | Il territorio del principato viene incorporato nella Francia rivoluzionaria |
| 1814 | I Grimaldi vengono restaurati dopo il periodo napoleonico |
| 1848 | Mentone e Roccabruna si dichiarano città libere sotto protezione sarda |
| 1861 | Mentone viene definitivamente incorporata nella Francia |

Non è quindi la semplice diffusione della Rivoluzione in una provincia già francese. Gli abitanti avevano rapporti propri con Monaco, i territori italiani vicini e l'amministrazione dei Grimaldi.

### Perché conta nella lettura

Per Jeanne, lealtà alla monarchia, identità e sicurezza sono strettamente connesse. Gabriel interpreta diversamente il cambiamento. Il contrasto acquista profondità in un territorio dal futuro politico incerto, non in un normale sfondo provinciale francese.

## 3. Ментон 1789 року: місто, яке не було французьким

Сьогодні Ментон розташований у департаменті Приморські Альпи, але на початку революції залежав від князівства Монако. Від придбання Карлом Грімальді у XIV столітті його політична історія була пов'язана з Монако та Рокбрюном. Наприкінці XVIII століття правив Оноре III: Франція мала значний вплив, але князівство зберігало окрему політичну ідентичність.

### Коротка хронологія

| Рік | Подія |
| --- | --- |
| 1346 | Ментон придбав Карл Грімальді, володар Монако |
| 1641 | Пероннський договір установив французький протекторат над князівством |
| 1789 | Почалася революція; Ментон ще належав до князівства |
| 1790 | Реформаторські рухи охопили Монако, Ментон і Рокбрюн |
| 1793 | Територію князівства включили до революційної Франції |
| 1814 | Після наполеонівського періоду владу Грімальді відновили |
| 1848 | Ментон і Рокбрюн оголосили себе вільними містами під сардинським захистом |
| 1861 | Ментон остаточно приєднали до Франції |

Тому поширення революційних ідей тут не було звичайною подією у французькій провінції. Мешканці мали власні відносини з Монако, сусідніми італійськими землями та адміністрацією Грімальді.

### Чому це важливо для читання

Для Жанни вірність монархії пов'язана з особистістю та безпекою. Ґабріель по-іншому сприймає зміни. Їхній конфлікт глибший, якщо пам'ятати: невизначеним було й політичне майбутнє всього краю.

## 4. Revolution beyond Paris: Monaco and the borderlands

The French Revolution is often remembered through Parisian events: the Bastille, the royal family, the National Assembly and the fall of the monarchy.

But revolutionary ideas didn't stop at the city limits.

They spread through correspondence, trade, military movements and political debate.

The small states and territories along the Mediterranean frontier were affected in different ways.

### The position of Honoré III

Prince Honoré III governed Monaco during the revolutionary era.

His position was increasingly difficult as demands for political reform spread.

Municipal reforms were introduced in 1790, but the relationship between the prince, his subjects and revolutionary developments remained unstable.

By 1793, the political order governing Menton had changed decisively.

### Was Menton simply a refuge from the Revolution?

Not entirely.

For a person fleeing Paris, Menton might have appeared geographically distant from the centre of revolutionary unrest.

But distance didn't guarantee safety or political neutrality.

The region had its own tensions, political loyalties and social divisions.

That is precisely what makes it an effective setting for a historical romance.

A character might escape immediate danger without escaping the questions that caused it.
fr:
## 4. La Révolution au-delà de Paris : Monaco et les frontières

La Bastille, la famille royale et l'Assemblée occupent souvent tout le récit de la Révolution. Pourtant, les idées circulent par les lettres, les échanges commerciaux, les déplacements militaires et les débats. Les petits territoires méditerranéens en ressentent les effets selon leur propre situation.

### La position d'Honoré III

Les demandes de réforme compliquent la position du prince. Des réformes municipales interviennent en 1790, mais les rapports entre pouvoir princier, habitants et bouleversements français restent instables. En 1793, l'ordre politique de Menton a profondément changé.

### Un refuge n'est pas une garantie de sécurité

S'éloigner de Paris peut réduire un danger immédiat sans supprimer les tensions, les fidélités contradictoires ou les divisions sociales. Le personnage peut quitter le centre de la crise sans échapper aux questions qui l'ont poussé à partir : un ressort fécond pour une romance historique, et non la preuve que la ville était politiquement neutre.

## 5. An artist at the end of the royal world

Jeanne Mercier is presented as a portrait painter connected with Marie Antoinette's court.

That gives her a distinctive place in the novel's historical imagination.

She is not simply a noblewoman fleeing political unrest.

Her position is connected with artistic skill and professional work.

Portraiture mattered enormously in eighteenth-century European court culture.

Paintings helped present the identities, status and authority of rulers and aristocrats.

Portrait artists worked within networks of commissions, patronage and personal reputation.

### Art and political change

The Revolution challenged the institutions that supported much court culture.

For an artist whose income and identity were closely connected with royal patronage, political upheaval could threaten both professional and personal security.

Jeanne's fictional circumstances allow the novel to explore this vulnerability.

But readers should distinguish the fictional character from historical artists who worked for Marie Antoinette.

In particular, Jeanne Mercier should not be confused with the celebrated real portraitist Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun.

Both belong to the broader subject of art and aristocratic patronage, but they are not the same person.

### A useful question while reading

What happens to an artist when the world that once valued their work begins to disappear?

This question gives the story a cultural dimension beyond the romantic plot.

Jeanne Mercier est présentée comme une portraitiste liée à la cour de Marie-Antoinette. Sa place ne tient donc pas seulement à un rang social : elle possède un métier et un talent. Au XVIIIe siècle, le portrait participe à la représentation de l'autorité, du statut et de l'identité ; les artistes dépendent de commandes, de protections et de leur réputation.

### L'art face au changement politique

Lorsque la Révolution remet en cause les institutions et les réseaux de la cour, une artiste peut perdre à la fois ses revenus, son entourage professionnel et une partie de sa sécurité. Le personnage permet de réfléchir à cette fragilité.

Jeanne reste une héroïne de fiction : ne la confondez pas avec Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun, portraitiste historique de Marie-Antoinette. Elles renvoient au même grand sujet du mécénat et de l'art de cour, mais ce ne sont pas la même personne.

### Une question à garder en tête

Que devient un artiste lorsque disparaît le monde qui reconnaissait son travail ? Cette interrogation élargit la lecture au-delà de l'histoire d'amour.

## 6. Lemons, markets and everyday eighteenth-century Menton

Menton's citrus heritage is one of its most familiar characteristics today.

But lemons were important to the local economy long before the modern Lemon Festival existed.

The region's climate allowed citrus cultivation alongside other Mediterranean agriculture.

The contrast between courtly society and everyday local life offers a useful reading lens. The accessible publisher and municipal descriptions do not independently verify Gabriel's precise occupation; this guide does not assign him one.

### Avoiding a modern misconception

Today's Fête du Citron is a twentieth-century celebration.

Its elaborate citrus sculptures and parade culture should not be projected backwards into 1789.

The eighteenth-century town knew lemons as agricultural products and elements of regional trade, not as the centrepiece of today's tourist festival.

### What about the market?

Menton's present municipal covered market is an attractive place to explore local food culture.

But the existing market building belongs to a much later period.

It is not the market structure Jeanne would have encountered in the fictional eighteenth-century setting.

A visit can still be worthwhile.

Just understand it as a modern connection with the town's continuing food traditions rather than a preserved scene from the novel.

## 7. The literary walk: looking for eighteenth-century Menton

The following walking route is inspired by the novel's historical setting.

It is not a reconstruction of Jeanne's movements or a claim that specific fictional scenes occurred at these precise addresses.

The available publisher and municipal descriptions establish Menton as an important setting, but they do not provide a reliable chapter-by-chapter map.

This itinerary instead focuses on historic streets, architecture and public spaces that help visitors imagine the city before its great nineteenth-century expansion.

### Stop 1. Rue Longue: entering the older town

Location: Rue Longue, Menton's historic centre.

Begin among the narrow streets of the old town.

This is the part of Menton where its pre-modern urban character is most apparent.

The buildings stand close together, with passages, stairways, small openings and changing views of the surrounding hills and sea.

These streets are more useful for imagining eighteenth-century Menton than the grand seafront hotels built much later.

### What to notice

Look at the scale of the streets.

Notice how buildings are arranged around pedestrian circulation rather than modern car traffic.

Look at the walls, stairs, shutters and passages.

Not every visible feature dates from the eighteenth century. Buildings have been renovated, façades altered and streets adapted.

But the old-town layout preserves something of the compact Mediterranean settlement.

Literary connection: The contrast between the courtly world Jeanne leaves behind and the smaller town where she seeks refuge.

### Stop 2. Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange: the town before the Revolution

Location: Parvis Saint-Michel.

Climb through the historic lanes towards the Basilica of Saint-Michel-Archange.

This is one of the most useful surviving landmarks for understanding Menton before the French Revolution.

The church was opened for worship in 1653 and consecrated in 1675.

Its great bell tower was begun in 1701, well before the novel's setting. Official descriptions differ on the completion year, so this guide does not select a precise end date.

These elements already belonged to the town's landscape by 1789.

However, the façade was completed in its later form in 1819, so the building visible today is not an unchanged eighteenth-century monument.

### What to do

Visit the square and admire the architecture.

If the church is open, explore the interior respectfully.

The square also provides a remarkable view across the old town and Mediterranean.

### Practical information

The municipal page publishes visiting times of Monday–Friday 15:00–17:00 and Saturday 10:00–12:00 and 15:00–17:00. Sunday 11:00 is a Mass, not an ordinary sightseeing slot. Services and exceptional closures may change access.

Check current arrangements before travelling.

The climb involves steep steps and slopes.

Literary connection: A historic religious landmark that genuinely existed in the period around the novel's setting, although later architectural changes must be recognised.

### Stop 3. The lower old town: everyday life beyond the palace

Descend towards the pedestrian streets below the basilica.

Rather than searching for a specific fictional house, use this part of the walk to think about ordinary eighteenth-century urban life.

Menton wasn't Versailles.

Its residents depended on agriculture, trade, services, crafts and networks of exchange with neighbouring territories.

The difference between social classes was significant.

For someone accustomed to court life, the experience of living in a smaller Mediterranean town could involve profound changes in daily routine, work and status.

This makes an interesting lens through which to interpret Jeanne's fictional circumstances.

Literary connection: The shift from aristocratic patronage towards the practical requirements of survival and independence.

### Stop 4. Marché des Halles: the continuity of local food culture

Location: Quai de Monléon.

Continue to Menton's covered municipal market.

The present building is not an eighteenth-century monument, but it offers a lively introduction to the area's food traditions.

Look for fruit, vegetables, olives, citrus products, cheese and other regional ingredients.

The sensory experience helps connect the modern town with a much older Mediterranean agricultural culture.

### What not to assume

The traders, stalls and current market building cannot be directly identified with the fictional market described in the novel.

Nor is the modern tourist economy a reconstruction of the 1789 town.

Think of this as a thematic stop, not an archaeological one.

Literary connection: Food, agriculture and the contrast between elite society and local everyday life.

### Stop 5. Les Sablettes and the old-town panorama: what changed?

Location: Esplanade des Sablettes.

Finish by looking back towards Menton's old town from the waterfront.

The colourful buildings rise above the sea, dominated by Saint-Michel.

It's one of the city's most memorable views.

But the modern esplanade, developed shoreline and many of the surrounding facilities belong to a much later era.

This is precisely why the viewpoint is useful.

It allows visitors to ask which features of the historic town have survived and which have been transformed.

The old town's silhouette gives a sense of continuity.

The seafront reveals how much has changed.

Literary connection: Menton as a real historical place that outlived the political world in which the novel takes place.

## 7. La promenade littéraire : chercher la Menton ancienne

Ce parcours s'inspire du cadre historique, pas d'une carte des déplacements de Jeanne. Les sources éditoriales et municipales situent bien le récit à Menton, sans fournir de correspondance fiable entre chapitres et adresses. Les cinq étapes aident à observer la ville antérieure à l'essor de la station balnéaire.

### Étape 1. Rue Longue : entrer dans le centre ancien

Commencez rue Longue. L'échelle resserrée des rues, les passages, escaliers et petites ouvertures disent davantage du vieux bourg que les grands hôtels côtiers construits plus tard. Regardez l'organisation des maisons, les volets, les murs et les vues qui changent à chaque détour.

Toutes les façades et tous les détails ne datent pas du XVIIIe siècle : restaurations et transformations se sont succédé. Le tissu urbain conserve néanmoins le caractère d'une petite implantation méditerranéenne. Lien de lecture : le contraste avec le monde de cour quitté par Jeanne.

### Étape 2. Saint-Michel-Archange : un repère antérieur à la Révolution

Montez vers le parvis Saint-Michel par les ruelles. L'église est ouverte au culte en 1653 et consacrée en 1675. Le grand campanile est commencé en 1701 : les descriptions officielles divergent sur l'année d'achèvement, que ce guide ne tranche pas. Il appartient en tout cas au paysage d'avant 1789.

La façade actuelle n'est terminée qu'en 1819. L'ensemble visible aujourd'hui n'est donc pas un monument du XVIIIe siècle resté intact. Admirez le parvis et la vue ; si l'intérieur est ouvert, visitez-le dans le respect du culte.

### Accès actuel

La page municipale annonce lundi–vendredi 15 h–17 h et samedi 10 h–12 h puis 15 h–17 h. Le dimanche à 11 h correspond à la messe, pas à un créneau de visite touristique. Offices et fermetures exceptionnelles peuvent modifier l'accès ; vérifiez avant de venir. La montée comporte de fortes pentes et des marches.

### Étape 3. Le bas de la vieille ville : vivre loin de la cour

Redescendez vers les rues piétonnes sous la basilique. Ne cherchez pas une maison fictive précise : pensez plutôt aux habitants vivant de l'agriculture, du commerce, des métiers et des services. Menton n'était pas Versailles. Les écarts sociaux et les exigences concrètes du quotidien donnent un autre sens à l'autonomie et à la survie d'une personne habituée au mécénat royal.

### Étape 4. Marché des Halles : la continuité alimentaire

Rejoignez les Halles, quai de Monléon. Fruits, légumes, olives, agrumes, fromages et produits régionaux relient la ville actuelle à de longues traditions méditerranéennes. Les étals, les commerçants et le bâtiment ne peuvent cependant pas être identifiés à ceux du roman. C'est une étape thématique, non archéologique ; privilégiez un passage quand le marché est ouvert.

### Étape 5. Les Sablettes : regarder ce qui a changé

Terminez sur l'esplanade des Sablettes et observez la vieille ville dominée par Saint-Michel. Sa silhouette suggère une continuité, tandis que l'esplanade aménagée et le rivage moderne rappellent les transformations. Le panorama sert à comparer les époques, pas à présenter le front de mer actuel comme celui de 1789.

## 7. La passeggiata letteraria: cercare la Mentone antica

L'itinerario si ispira al contesto storico, non ricostruisce gli spostamenti di Jeanne. Le descrizioni editoriali e municipali confermano il ruolo di Mentone, senza offrire una mappa attendibile capitolo per capitolo. Le cinque tappe suggeriscono dove osservare il tessuto della città precedente allo sviluppo ottocentesco.

### Tappa 1. Rue Longue: entrare nel centro antico

Comincia da Rue Longue. Strade strette, passaggi, scalinate e aperture verso mare e colline raccontano il vecchio insediamento meglio dei grandi alberghi successivi. Osserva la scala delle case, i muri, le persiane e l'organizzazione degli spazi pedonali.

Non ogni facciata o dettaglio risale al Settecento: edifici e strade sono stati restaurati e modificati. L'impianto conserva tuttavia qualcosa della piccola città mediterranea. Collegamento letterario: la distanza tra questo ambiente e la corte lasciata da Jeanne.

### Tappa 2. Saint-Michel-Archange: un riferimento anteriore alla Rivoluzione

Sali per i vicoli fino al sagrato. La chiesa fu aperta al culto nel 1653 e consacrata nel 1675. Il grande campanile fu iniziato nel 1701; le descrizioni ufficiali divergono sull'anno di completamento, che questa guida non stabilisce. Apparteneva comunque al paesaggio precedente al 1789.

La facciata attuale fu terminata nel 1819: l'insieme non è un monumento settecentesco rimasto immutato. Ammira architettura e panorama; entra con rispetto se la chiesa è aperta.

### Accesso attuale

La pagina comunale pubblica lunedì–venerdì 15:00–17:00 e sabato 10:00–12:00 e 15:00–17:00. La domenica alle 11:00 è prevista la Messa, non una normale visita turistica. Funzioni e chiusure eccezionali possono modificare l'accesso: controlla prima di partire. La salita comprende pendenze marcate e gradini.

### Tappa 3. La parte bassa del centro antico: vivere lontano dalla corte

Scendi verso le strade pedonali sotto la basilica. Invece di cercare una precisa casa immaginaria, pensa ad agricoltura, scambi, mestieri e servizi. Mentone non era Versailles. Le differenze sociali e le esigenze pratiche del quotidiano offrono una chiave per leggere l'indipendenza e la sopravvivenza di chi dipendeva dal mecenatismo reale.

### Tappa 4. Marché des Halles: continuità della cultura alimentare

Prosegui alle Halles sul Quai de Monléon. Frutta, verdura, olive, agrumi, formaggi e ingredienti regionali collegano la città moderna a tradizioni mediterranee più antiche. Né i commercianti né i banchi o l'edificio possono essere identificati con quelli del romanzo. È una tappa tematica, non archeologica; scegli un momento in cui il mercato è aperto.

### Tappa 5. Les Sablettes: osservare ciò che è cambiato

Concludi sull'Esplanade des Sablettes guardando il centro antico dominato da Saint-Michel. La sagoma suggerisce continuità, mentre passeggiata, strutture e litorale moderno mostrano quanto sia cambiato il paesaggio. Il panorama serve a confrontare epoche, non a ricostruire il lungomare del 1789.

## 7. Літературна прогулянка: шукаємо давній Ментон

Маршрут натхнений історичним тлом, не відтворює пересування Жанни. Видавнича й міська публікації підтверджують значення Ментона, але не дають надійної карти розділів та адрес. П'ять зупинок допоможуть побачити структуру міста до його розширення у XIX столітті.

### Зупинка 1. Rue Longue: вхід до старого міста

Почніть із Rue Longue. Вузькі вулиці, проходи, сходи й просвіти до моря та пагорбів більше розповідають про давнє поселення, ніж пізніші курортні готелі. Придивіться до масштабу будинків, стін, віконниць і пішохідної організації простору.

Не всі фасади й деталі походять із XVIII століття: будинки та вулиці змінювали й реставрували. Проте планування зберігає характер компактного середземноморського міста. Літературний зв'язок: контраст із придворним світом, який залишила Жанна.

### Зупинка 2. Saint-Michel-Archange: орієнтир до революції

Підніміться провулками до площі перед базилікою. Церкву відкрили для богослужінь 1653 року й освятили 1675-го. Велику дзвіницю почали будувати 1701 року; офіційні описи розходяться щодо року завершення, тому гайд його не обирає. Вона в будь-якому разі належала до краєвиду до 1789 року.

Нинішній фасад завершили лише 1819 року. Отже, перед нами не незмінна пам'ятка XVIII століття. Помилуйтеся архітектурою та видом; якщо церква відкрита, огляньте її з повагою до богослужінь.

### Нинішній доступ

## 9. What kind of reader will enjoy Les Derniers Feux de la royauté?

This novel will particularly appeal to readers who enjoy historical romance with a strong sense of place.

### Readers of French historical romance

The relationship between characters from opposing political and social worlds provides the central romantic tension.

The novel belongs to a genre in which personal relationships unfold against major historical events.

### Readers interested in the French Revolution

The story introduces a less familiar geographical perspective on the revolutionary period.

Instead of remaining exclusively in Paris, it brings the political uncertainty of 1789 to the Mediterranean borderlands.

However, anyone seeking a detailed academic account of the Revolution should read historical research alongside it.

### Readers who enjoy regional fiction

Virginie Platel's attachment to Menton gives the novel a particularly local purpose.

She researched the town's historical setting and aimed to evoke its landscapes, scents and everyday life.

### Readers interested in women and artistic professions

Jeanne's identity as a portraitist adds another dimension to the historical romance.

Her professional skills are part of the fictional world, not merely decorative background.

### Who might prefer another book?

If you primarily enjoy archival history, footnoted nonfiction or strictly documentary accounts, this may not be your first choice.

The novel is designed as historical romance.

Its aim is to tell an engaging story within a researched setting, not to provide a complete scholarly reconstruction of Menton in 1789.

## 10. Why this novel shouldn't be read as documentary history

Historical fiction can be a wonderful introduction to the past.

But several distinctions matter.

| Element | How to interpret it |
| --- | --- |
| French Revolution beginning in 1789 | Documented historical event |
| Menton's relationship with Monaco | Documented political history |
| Prince Honoré III | Historical figure |
| Local citrus cultivation | Historical economic context |
| Jeanne Mercier | Fictional protagonist |
| Gabriel | Fictional protagonist |
| Their conversations and relationship | Literary invention |
| Particular houses and private encounters | Require evidence before treating as historical fact |
| Today's old-town buildings | Mixture of historic fabric and later changes |

The author's use of archival research gives the setting greater credibility.

It does not turn every fictional episode into evidence.

A historical novel can compress time, invent characters and rearrange events to develop a narrative.

A traveller interested in the actual political history of Menton should therefore distinguish the literary experience from the historical record.

### Where to research further

The City of Menton maintains municipal archives, including an ancient collection covering documents from before 1794.

The municipal library also holds historical resources relevant to local research. The municipal archives are a separate service: consult the catalogue and arrange an appointment rather than treating them as an unannounced walking-tour stop.

For readers who want to investigate eighteenth-century Menton, these institutional collections are more appropriate primary starting points than the novel alone.

[Municipal archives: collections and appointments](https://www.menton.fr/les-archives-municipales.html)

## 10. Pourquoi ne pas le lire comme un documentaire ?

La fiction peut donner envie d'étudier le passé, à condition de distinguer ses matériaux.

| Élément | Comment le comprendre |
| --- | --- |
| Début de la Révolution en 1789 | Événement historique documenté |
| Relation de Menton avec Monaco | Histoire politique documentée |
| Le prince Honoré III | Personnage historique |
| Culture locale des agrumes | Contexte économique historique |
| Jeanne Mercier | Héroïne de fiction |
| Gabriel | Personnage de fiction |
| Leurs dialogues et leur relation | Invention romanesque |
| Maisons et rencontres privées précises | Nécessitent des preuves avant toute lecture historique |
| Bâtiments actuels du centre ancien | Tissu ancien mêlé à des transformations ultérieures |

Une recherche de l'auteure ne prouve pas chaque conversation ni chaque adresse. La lecture littéraire et l'enquête historique restent complémentaires.

### Où prolonger la recherche ?

Les archives municipales possèdent un fonds ancien antérieur à 1794. La bibliothèque conserve également des ressources locales, mais il s'agit de services distincts. Consultez les catalogues et prenez rendez-vous pour les archives : ce n'est pas une étape où entrer à l'improviste pendant la promenade.

[Archives municipales : fonds et rendez-vous](https://www.menton.fr/les-archives-municipales.html)

## 10. Perché non leggerlo come un documentario?

La narrativa può essere un ottimo invito a conoscere il passato, purché si distinguano le sue componenti.

| Elemento | Come interpretarlo |
| --- | --- |
| Inizio della Rivoluzione nel 1789 | Evento storico documentato |
| Rapporto di Mentone con Monaco | Storia politica documentata |
| Principe Onorato III | Figura storica |
| Coltivazione locale degli agrumi | Contesto economico storico |
| Jeanne Mercier | Protagonista immaginaria |
| Gabriel | Personaggio immaginario |
| Conversazioni e relazione | Invenzione narrativa |
| Case e incontri privati precisi | Richiedono prove prima di essere trattati come fatti |
| Edifici attuali del centro antico | Tessuto storico e trasformazioni successive |

La ricerca dell'autrice non documenta ogni dialogo e ogni indirizzo. Esperienza letteraria e indagine storica restano distinte e complementari.

### Dove proseguire le ricerche?

Gli archivi comunali conservano un fondo antico anteriore al 1794. Anche la biblioteca possiede risorse locali, ma è un servizio diverso. Consulta i cataloghi e prenota un appuntamento agli archivi: non considerarli una tappa dove presentarti senza preavviso durante la passeggiata.

Художня проза може заохотити до вивчення минулого, якщо розрізняти її складники.

Міські архіви мають давній фонд із документами до 1794 року. Бібліотека також зберігає місцеві ресурси, але це інша установа. Перегляньте каталоги й домовтеся про візит до архівів: це не місце, куди слід заходити без попередження під час прогулянки.

## 11. Menton before the Belle Époque

One reason this book is a valuable addition to the AzurMenton literary collection is that it explores a period often overlooked by visitors.

Many familiar stories about Menton belong to the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

The British winter visitors.

The grand hotels.

Katherine Mansfield.

Jean Cocteau.

The spectacular gardens.

The Lemon Festival.

But Les Derniers Feux de la royauté directs attention to an earlier city.

A Menton connected to Monaco and the Grimaldis.

A region shaped by Mediterranean trade and agricultural life.

A time when revolutionary ideas were challenging established political arrangements.

For readers who already know modern Menton, the contrast is fascinating.

The town's beauty may seem familiar.

Its historical identity is less so.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Les Derniers Feux de la royauté set in Menton?

Yes. Menton is an important setting in the historical romance, following Jeanne Mercier's departure from Paris during the revolutionary period.

### Who wrote Les Derniers Feux de la royauté?

French author and screenwriter Virginie Platel, who grew up in Menton.

### When was the novel published?

It was published on 1 July 2020 by Harlequin, in the Aliénor historical romance collection.

### Is Jeanne Mercier a real historical portraitist?

The character is presented as a fictional protagonist. She should not be identified with a documented royal portraitist without independent historical evidence.

### Was Menton part of France in 1789?

No. Menton was part of the territory associated with the Principality of Monaco under the Grimaldi dynasty. Its political status changed during the Revolution, and it became definitively French in 1861.

### Did the author research Menton's history?

Yes. The City of Menton reports that Platel consulted the Octobon collection through the municipal library while researching the eighteenth-century setting.

### Can you visit locations from the novel?

You can explore the town's historic environment, including older streets and the Basilica of Saint-Michel. However, this guide does not claim that specific fictional scenes took place at the suggested stops.

### Is the modern covered market from the eighteenth century?

No. Today's market building belongs to a later period. It is included as a thematic stop connected with local food culture.

### Is the walking route suitable for wheelchair users?

The upper old town includes steep stairs and uneven surfaces. The full route is not step-free. Visitors with reduced mobility should choose a suitable lower-town alternative.

### Is this guide spoiler-free?

Yes. It introduces the novel's premise, setting and historical context without revealing major developments or the ending.

### Le roman se déroule-t-il à Menton ?

Oui, la ville constitue un cadre important après le départ de Jeanne Mercier de Paris, d'après la présentation municipale.

### Qui l'a écrit ?

Virginie Platel, auteure et scénariste française qui a grandi à Menton.

Le 1er juillet 2020 chez Harlequin, collection Aliénor, en français.

Elle est présentée ici comme une héroïne de fiction, pas comme une artiste réelle attestée ni comme Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun.

### Menton était-elle française en 1789 ?

Non : elle appartenait à la principauté de Monaco. Son statut change pendant la Révolution ; le rattachement définitif à la France date de 1861.

La Ville indique qu'elle a consulté le fonds Octobon grâce à la bibliothèque municipale pour son cadre du XVIIIe siècle.

### Peut-on visiter les lieux précis des scènes ?

On peut explorer l'environnement historique, pas vérifier chaque scène aux adresses proposées par ce guide.

Non. Elles servent de lien thématique avec les traditions alimentaires, non de décor intact du roman.

### Le parcours est-il adapté au fauteuil roulant ?

L'itinéraire complet n'est pas sans marches : fortes pentes, escaliers et surfaces irrégulières dans le haut du centre ancien. Préférez une alternative adaptée dans le bas de la ville.

Non. Il expose la situation initiale et le contexte sans révéler les grands développements ni le dénouement.

## Domande frequenti

### Il romanzo è ambientato a Mentone?

Sì, secondo la presentazione comunale è un luogo importante dopo la partenza di Jeanne Mercier da Parigi.

### Chi lo ha scritto?

Virginie Platel, scrittrice e sceneggiatrice francese cresciuta a Mentone.

### Quando è uscito?

Il 1° luglio 2020 per Harlequin, collana Aliénor, in francese.

### Jeanne Mercier è una vera ritrattista storica?

Qui è presentata come protagonista immaginaria, non come un'artista documentata o come Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun.

### Mentone era francese nel 1789?

No: faceva parte del Principato di Monaco. Lo status cambiò durante la Rivoluzione; il passaggio definitivo alla Francia risale al 1861.

### L'autrice ha fatto ricerche?

Il Comune riferisce che consultò il fondo Octobon grazie alla biblioteca municipale per ricostruire il contesto settecentesco.

### Si possono visitare gli indirizzi delle singole scene?

Si può esplorare l'ambiente storico, non verificare ogni scena presso gli indirizzi suggeriti dalla guida.

### Le Halles attuali risalgono al Settecento?

No. Sono un collegamento tematico con la cultura alimentare, non un ambiente intatto del romanzo.

### Il percorso è adatto alla sedia a rotelle?

Il percorso completo non è senza gradini: il centro alto comprende scale ripide e superfici irregolari. Scegli un'alternativa adatta nella parte bassa.

### La guida svela il finale?

No. Introduce premessa e contesto senza le principali svolte o il finale.

## Поширені запитання

### Події роману відбуваються в Ментоні?

Так, за міською публікацією це важливе місце після від'їзду Жанни Мерсьє з Парижа.

### Хто написав книжку?

Віржині Платель, французька письменниця й сценаристка, яка виросла в Ментоні.

### Коли вона вийшла?

1 липня 2020 року у Harlequin, серія Aliénor, французькою.

### Жанна Мерсьє — реальна історична портретистка?

Тут її представлено вигаданою героїнею, не документованою художницею й не Елізабет Віже-Лебрен.

### Ментон був французьким 1789 року?

Ні, він належав до князівства Монако. Статус змінювався під час революції; остаточне приєднання до Франції відбулося 1861 року.

### Авторка досліджувала історію?

Місто повідомляє, що вона працювала з фондом Octobon завдяки муніципальній бібліотеці для відтворення тла XVIII століття.

### Можна відвідати точні адреси сцен?

Можна дослідити історичне середовище, але цей гайд не підтверджує окремих сцен за запропонованими адресами.

### Сучасні Halles походять із XVIII століття?

Ні. Це тематичний зв'язок із харчовими традиціями, а не незмінний декор роману.

### Маршрут підходить для крісла колісного?

Повний маршрут не безсходинковий: нагорі є круті сходи й нерівні поверхні. Оберіть відповідну альтернативу в нижній частині міста.

### Гайд розкриває фінал?

Ні. Він подає початкову ситуацію та контекст без головних поворотів і розв'язки.

## Final thoughts: a different Menton behind the familiar façades

Menton is often presented through images of sunshine, gardens and the Mediterranean.

Those images are beautiful.

But they represent only part of the town's history.

In Les Derniers Feux de la royauté, Virginie Platel takes readers back to a period when the political future of Menton was uncertain and the French Revolution was transforming the world beyond its borders.

The fictional story brings together a woman associated with the royal court and a man drawn towards revolutionary ideas.

Their relationship offers a personal way into a much larger historical moment.

For visitors today, the novel provides a reason to look at Menton's old town differently.

To notice the buildings that stood before the nineteenth-century resort.

To consider the relationship with Monaco.

And to remember that the streets we walk through today have witnessed more than holidays and beautiful sunsets.

The Riviera has always been a place where different worlds meet.

In 1789, those differences could change the course of a life.
